title: Chicken Fricassee With Vermouth
description: By Craig Claiborne and Pierre Franey, Updated July 2, 2024. This is an elegant, velvety take on a traditional skillet-supper, perfect with a mound of fluffy white rice or wide broad noodles or luscious mashed potatoes. Cooking this fricassee with the aperitif known as dry vermouth instead of the more traditional white wine results in a slightly sweeter and more aromatic sauce than you would ordinarily get. (White vermouth is composed of, among other things, white wine plus a bit of sugar, herbs and plants and, at times, the bark of trees.) But white wine will work as well.
ingredients: 1 three-and-one-half-pound chicken, cut into serving pieces, or skin-on thighs, 1-2 per person
2 sprigs fresh thyme or ½ teaspoon dried
1 cup carrots cut into fine, julienne strips, about two inches long
1½ cups loosely packed leeks cut into fine, julienne strips, about three inches long
directions: Sprinkle the chicken with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat the butter in a skillet and add the chicken pieces skin side down. Cook over moderate heat about one minute without browning.
Scatter the onion over all and cook 30 seconds. Add the garlic and stir it around. Cook the chicken about four minutes, turning the pieces often in the butter.
Sprinkle the flour over all, turning the pieces so that they are evenly coated. Add the vermouth, chicken broth, bay leaf and thyme. Cover and cook over moderate heat about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring some water to boil for the carrots and leeks. Drop the leeks in first, then after 3 minutes add the carrots and boil for another minute, or four minutes total. Then drain the pot.
When the chicken has cooked for a total of 30 minutes (start to finish), add the carrots, leeks and cream. Let simmer about two minutes. Serve with rice or noodles or potatoes.
